'''Jean-Pierre Wintenberger''' (1954 – 23 January 2019) was a French [[mathematician]] and a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Strasbourg]]. He was corecipient of the 2011 [[Cole Prize]] in [[number theory]], along with [[Chandrashekhar Khare]], for his proof of [[Serre conjecture (number theory)|Serre's modularity conjecture]].<ref>{{cite web|title=January 2011 Prizes and Awards|website=ams.org|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/prize-booklet-2011.pdf|page=54|access-date=6 May 2024|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000923/http://www.ams.org/profession/prize-booklet-2011.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Wintenberger earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] at [[Joseph Fourier University]] in 1984, under supervision of [[Jean-Marc Fontaine]].

Wintenberger died on 23 January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/insmi/spip.php?article3063|title=Décès de Jean-Pierre Wintenberger|date=20 March 2024|website=www.insmi.cnrs.fr|language=fr|access-date=26 January 2019|archive-date=28 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128155346/http://www.cnrs.fr/insmi/spip.php?article3063|url-status=dead}}</ref>
